reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund data myself, since the handoff from W2 is only a summary and payouts can't be undone.
Before paying, I need to verify the refunds myself. W2's summary only lists three refunds, and I should confirm they match the shared ledger before computing any balances.
The refunds match W2's summary exactly, and each refund is smaller than its order, so I found no concrete problem. I'll get the net balance for each customer from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net of 33841 matches what I compute from the orders (32343 + 11079) minus its refund on order 193 (9581), so the figure checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 34692 matches the orders (26465 + 14199) minus the order 194 refund (5972), so it checks out. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 18779 matches orders 192 + 195 (19506 + 2421 = 21927) minus the order 192 refund (3148). All three balances check out against the orders and refunds, so I'll record payouts, starting with acme at 33841.
Acme's payout recorded successfully. Birch's net of 34692 matches its orders (26465 + 14199 = 40664) minus the order 194 refund (5972), so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout was recorded successfully. Cobalt is the last customer, and its net of 18779 matches orders 192 and 195 (21927) minus the order 192 refund (3148), so I'll record that payout.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each amount matched the net balance returned by net_balance and my check against the orders and refunds. The batch is complete.
